transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-20
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Pacifica CTO), Rina Shah (Pacifica Cloud Ops), Omar Delgado (Pacifica Security), Priya Menon (Pacifica ML)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Luis and Asha from our engineering team. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Daniel Park: Doing good, thanks. Busy week but excited to chat.
[00:08] Luis Ortega: Great, I'll give a quick agenda — cover our Private/VPC deployment options, typical network topologies (VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink/private endpoints, transit gateway), what customers usually do for region constraints, and then we can drill into Pacifica's constraints.
[00:18] Rina Shah: That sounds good. We're mainly worried about data residency and strict no-internet-access for inference endpoints. Also CIDR collisions, and we have multiple AWS accounts per BU.
[00:26] Asha Patel: Totally — we see that a lot. Just to set expectations: Redwood Private can be deployed with a control plane in your account or our managed control plane depending on enterprise terms, and compute nodes can either sit in your VPC or in a customer-dedicated VPC with peering — we can map both out.
[00:40] Omar Delgado: Quick security question: do you support bringing our own KMS and HSM? All keys must be customer-managed.
[00:46] Maya Chen: Yes, BYOK is supported. We integrate with KMS providers; HSM integrations are part of our enterprise bundle. We'll share the SOC2 doc and KMS integration guide after the call.
[00:54] Priya Menon: For the model serving — how do you handle private endpoints? We need the inference endpoints to be accessible only from our VPCs and only via private IPs.
[01:02] Luis Ortega: We support two common patterns: 1) VPC peering or Transit Gateway where compute sits in Redwood-managed VPCs and you peer from your VPCs; or 2) deploy the compute inside your VPC using our private deployment agent/container — that gives you full control of network egress. For private endpoints, we expose service endpoints via PrivateLink (AWS NLB with private IPs) which you can attach to your VPC.
[01:20] Daniel Park: Hmm, with PrivateLink do we need to open internet egress for downloading models or updates?
[01:25] Luis Ortega: Good question. Model downloads and updates can be routed through a restricted egress path — we can provide a proxy or use S3 endpoints with VPC endpoints. In the fully private option (compute in your VPC), you control the egress; in the managed option we use peering plus a narrowly scoped egress for patching and model fetching.
[01:40] Rina Shah: Our primary blocker is CIDR overlap — multiple teams use 10.0.0.0/8 derivatives so peering breaks. Transit gateway is costy. Do you have examples for cross-account peering?
[01:50] Asha Patel: Yes — we've done cross-account peering with route filters and prefix lists to avoid overlap. For customers with heavy overlap, we often recommend PrivateLink (it doesn't require overlapping CIDRs) or bringing compute into customer VPCs. We'll send sample terraform for both.
[02:05] Omar Delgado: What about region constraints — we need all data and inference to run in us-east-1 only. Any region availability issues?
[02:12] Luis Ortega: We have dedicated capacity and Private deployment options in us-east-1; most enterprise customers pin their compute region. If you need multi-AZ but single-region, that's easily supported. The only caveat is if you want disaster failover cross-region, that'll require replication and a DR plan.
[02:27] Daniel Park: For latency-sensitive features, we have models with short prompt sizes — what's the latency profile on dedicated vs hosted?
[02:32] Maya Chen: Typically hosted API has slightly higher variability because of multi-tenant queuing, but our Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments are tuned for low latency — customers see 30-60% lower p99 latency when running on pinned dedicated nodes. We can share perf profiles per model.
[02:45] Priya Menon: Any constraints around KV cache or continuous batching when running in a private VPC?
[02:50] Luis Ortega: No — those runtime optimizations are part of the serving runtime and ship with both managed and private deployments. The only difference is control over memory footprint and kernel tuning if you self-host.
[03:02] Rina Shah: About networking specifics: do you use static IP ranges for your private endpoints? We need to allow-list IPs at the firewall.
[03:08] Luis Ortega: Yes, we can supply stable IP ranges for NLB endpoints, and for managed peering we provide the peer IP blocks. If you run compute in your VPC, the endpoints will be your own IPs.
[03:18] Maya Chen: Also, for compliance we offer audit logs and request tracing shipped to your S3 or cloud logging — we'll include that in the security pack.
[03:25] Omar Delgado: How is authentication handled — SSO, SAML, RBAC?
[03:29] Asha Patel: We support SAML/SSO and role-based access controls. For private deployments we can integrate with your IdP directly. API keys still exist for service-to-service calls but can be rotated via our APIs and tied to roles.
[03:40] Daniel Park: Ok. Pricing question: if we run private in our VPC with dedicated capacity, is pricing usage-based or a fixed reservation?
[03:46] Maya Chen: For Dedicated/Private, it's typically reserved capacity with monthly or annual commitments plus a smaller per-token usage charge for burst. We'll send an initial pricing sheet, but figure we should size the pilot first.
[03:55] Priya Menon: For a pilot, can we run a small fleet in our VPC for 2-4 weeks to run latency and cost benchmarks?
[04:02] Luis Ortega: Absolutely. We usually do a 2-4 week pilot with a few instances sized to your expected qps. We'll need your VPC details, CIDR blocks, and sample traffic patterns.
[04:12] Rina Shah: We'll need a network diagram that shows where Redwood control plane sits and what ports need to be open. Also NAT/egress considerations.
[04:19] Maya Chen: We'll attach a sample network diagram and a list of required ports. The typical ports are 443 for control traffic and optional ephemeral ranges for model updates if you allow egress.
[04:28] Daniel Park: Any S3 integration for model artifacts with KMS encryption?
[04:31] Luis Ortega: Yes, you can provide an S3 bucket with KMS CMKs; we can pull model artifacts from your S3 via VPC endpoints, no internet required.
[04:38] Omar Delgado: Auditability is critical — we need full request tracing and retention of logs for 12 months. Is that supported?
[04:44] Asha Patel: Yes, we support configurable retention and ship logs to your S3 or your SIEM via secure forwarders. We'll include sample retention settings.
[04:52] Priya Menon: On the topic of model versions and rollouts — can you pin model versions and roll back quickly?
[04:58] Maya Chen: Yes, rollout controls (canary/AB/fallback) are supported in Private. We keep model versions in a catalog and have fast rollbacks.
[05:07] Rina Shah: For account separation, we want per-BU isolation and per-team RBAC. What's the recommended approach?
[05:12] Asha Patel: Many customers use separate subnets and separate compute clusters per BU, plus RBAC in the control plane. If you want stronger isolation, we can do separate clusters in separate AWS accounts.
[05:24] Daniel Park: Great. Can you send us example terraform for both the PrivateLink and in-VPC deploy patterns?
[05:29] Luis Ortega: Will do. We'll include the NLB config, required route tables, and prefix list examples.
[05:35] Omar Delgado: One last question: are you able to provide a temporary dedicated capacity option for benchmarking without long-term commitment?
[05:40] Maya Chen: Yes, we can offer a time-boxed pilot with a short-term commitment for benchmarking. Pricing will be slightly higher but it's typical for pilots.
[05:48] Maya Chen: Ok let's recap next steps — we'll: 1) Send security pack (SOC2, KMS guide, audit log examples), 2) Share terraform and network diagrams for PrivateLink and in-VPC deploy, 3) Schedule technical deep-dive for 2027-04-26, and 4) get Pacifica to share VPC CIDRs and expected qps.
[06:05] Daniel Park: Sounds good. Rina will send CIDRs and we'll confirm the deep dive attendees.
[06:10] Rina Shah: Yep, I'll send them by end of tomorrow.
[06:13] Priya Menon: I'll prepare sample traffic for the pilot and share via the ticket.
[06:16] Maya Chen: Perfect. Thank you all, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[06:20] End of meeting

Notes on transcription: occasional overlaps, some brand names transcribed imperfectly (e.g., 'PrivateLink' sometimes shows as 'private link'), minor filler words removed for readability. Links shared in chat: Security whitepaper: https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/security/pacifica/security-pack.pdf ; Example terraform repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-examples
